newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal deplores expulsion of envoy from S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Portugal deplores expulsion of envoy from S.Africa.

text.p: Portugal deplored on Monday the expulsion of its ambassador from South Africa over the leaking of a misdirected note from President Nelson Mandela to Indonesian President Suharto.
Mandela had written to President Suharto in mid-July, asking him to release East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao, according to South African sources.
The letter was sent in error to the embassy of Portugal -- the former colonial power in East Timor -- and was neither returned nor forwarded to the Indonesian embassy.
The Portuguese government called in the South African ambassador and asked him to explain the expulsion.

"The South African ambassador was called to the Foreign Ministry today where the government told him that it energetically deplored the way in which South Africa treated the Portuguese ambassador in Pretoria," a government statement said.

Mandela's proposal was leaked to newspapers in Portugal before Suharto was made aware of it and the incident bruised his attempt to bolster a United Nations effort to resolve the conflict over Indonesia's disputed rule in East Timor.

The South African sources said the incident had not permanently damaged relations with Indonesia or Portugal, but the expulsion of Ambassador Vasco Valente was the first time South Africa had expelled a diplomat since Mandela became its first democratically elected leader in 1994.

Portugal also protested at the way South Africa had responded to explanations for the so-called misunderstanding between the Portuguese embassy and the South African presidency, the government statement said.

"Such an attitude is even more incomprehensible when the Portuguese authorities, namely the President and the government, responded positively to an initiative of President Mandela on East Timor," it said.
In Pretoria at the end of last month, Mandela briefed Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio on his initiative to settle a dispute over the Pacific territory of East Timor.
Mandela, whose release in 1990 after 27 years in jail paved the way to a peaceful settlement in South Africa four years later, met Gusmao during a recent visit to Indonesia.
He has since invited Suharto to visit South Africa in November, following a proposed visit by East Timorese bishop and Nobel peace laureate Ximenes Belo in October.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan will see Mandela on Friday to discuss their joint initiative for peace in East Timor.
Ambassadorial-level talks between Indonesia and Portugal on the question of East Timor opened on Monday at U.N. headquarters.

Indonesia entered the territory in 1975 after Portugal relinquished colonial rule in 1974, and a small group of armed guerrillas are still fighting Indonesian rule, which is not recognised by the United Nations.
